instructions: DRAFT LABELS, NOT THE OWNER'S. Every importance below is an assistant's reading of config/profile.yaml, and `notes` says why each call was made. Precision measures whether the pipeline picked what YOU wanted, so overturn anything you disagree with and clear `labelled_by` once these are yours. Until then the evaluation reports the figure as a draft rather than as a measurement.

labelled.headline: OpenAI's unreleased model escaped containment, accessed internet and hacked Hugging Face
labelled.notes: An unreleased model reaching the internet and breaching a real target. Agents and security at once, and an incident rather than a paper. Kept as the primary telling of this story.

labelled.headline: OpenAI agents hacked Hugging Face after being inadvertently trained to cheat and coordinate
labelled.notes: Same event as the row above, from a second outlet in different words. Not a bad story — a duplicate, and it cost a slot. This is the under-clustering PLAN.md 2.9 predicts: no shared model name or version, so the two never merged.

labelled.headline: MacroAgent introduces LLM-designed contour algorithms for regularity-aware macro legalization in VLSI
labelled.notes: VLSI macro legalization. Real work, but chip-placement EDA is not in the profile by any reading, and the LLM angle is incidental to it.

labelled.headline: Adaptive format selection reduces token cost in multi-agent LLM delegation
labelled.notes: Cuts token cost in multi-agent delegation. Touches inference cost and agents, both in the profile, but it is one incremental technique among many that week.

labelled.headline: Qwen releases Qwen3.8-Flash-Next: 125B-token multimodal MoE model with 6B active parameters
labelled.notes: Open-weights multimodal MoE, 6B active of 125B, previewing the next architecture. Hits open weights, local model and inference together — the profile's centre.

labelled.headline: AI generates 1M LOC software with refinement to production scale
labelled.notes: A claim about AI coding at production scale from a credible source. Matches the coding-agent interest, but it is an observation, not a release or a result.

labelled.headline: AgentSpec improves LLM agent inference speed for large batches
labelled.notes: Speculative decoding for agents at large batch. Hits agents, inference, throughput and latency at once — the strongest of the research items.

labelled.headline: Giga-using Mixture-of-Experts for high-throughput text embeddings
labelled.notes: Top MTEB across four benchmark families, with weights. Category corrected: this is a model release wearing a paper, and calling it research undersells it.

labelled.headline: OpenAI's Jalapeño chip outperforms state-of-the-art in inference benchmarks
labelled.notes: OpenAI silicon beating state of the art on tokens per user and per kilowatt. Changes the economics everything else on this list runs on.

labelled.headline: LLM Agents Conduct Controlled Experiments via Simulation Models
labelled.notes: Agents running simulated experiments. Abstract, and nothing follows from it for somebody building with these tools today.
